analyticalQuestion: Which parts of the deviatoric high-high contraction vanish under helicity or angular averaging, and how do the surviving source-core norms scale?
takeaway: A pure helical mode can have pointwise coupling one with an STF source; the complete sphere cancels only the signed quadrupole while its positive part has mean sqrt(3)/9; and the critical source and core dual norms scale oppositely with a scale-invariant pairing.

panels.question: Does fixed helicity force the STF contraction to vanish through phase?
panels.takeaway: For S0 and either helicity the contraction is identically one; a trace-free control can have zero phase mean without being pointwise zero.

panels.question: What remains after a complete isotropic angular average?
panels.takeaway: The signed mean of P2(z) is zero, but the normalized positive-part mean is sqrt(3)/9.

panels.question: How do the source square norm, core dual square norm, and their pairing transform across scale?
panels.takeaway: At amplitude a=1, after normalizing fixed profile, time-integral, and Lambda factors, source norm squared scales as r, the core dual norm squared as r^(-1), and both the Cauchy product and signed pairing stay scale invariant.
